sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
Now G count is 9, b count 52. Need 53 more G. This is a lot but doable. Since time limited, we can continue clicking leftmost b repeatedly. We can attempt to click many times in a batch but earlier batch only executed first action. Perhaps because after first action, the state changes and the remaining actions are considered known from that new state? Actually the system may stop batch when it encounters an action that was already tried from that state (including same coordinate). Since we always click same coordinate (col1), after first click, clicking col1 again is a new action? It might be considered same action from new state, but maybe the graph marks that action as tried already (since we clicked col1 before from previous state). However after state changes, the action is still MOUSE at same coordinate, but it's a different state, so should be untried. But maybe the system treats actions globally not per-state? Might be that MOUSE action is considered same regardless of state, so after first click, subsequent MOUSE actions are considered already tried globally and thus rejected. That's why batch stops after first. So we need to vary the coordinate each time to be considered new action. So we can click successive b positions moving rightwards. That will be new coordinates each time. So we can batch a sequence of clicks across the line from leftmost to rightmost b. That will be at most 62 actions. That's okay.
We can generate actions for all remaining b positions in order left to right. Let's do that.

sections.content:

<function=python>
<parameter=code>
row = current_frame.ascii.split('\n')[1]
b_positions = [i for i,ch in enumerate(row) if ch=='b']
print('remaining b', len(b_positions))
actions = [{'action':'MOUSE','row':1,'col':col} for col in b_positions]
# execute in batches of maybe 20 to avoid timeout
batch=20
for i in range(0,len(actions),batch):
    batch_actions = actions[i:i+batch]
    action(batch_actions)
    # check if level completed
    if last_action_result.get('level_completed') or last_action_result.get('done'):
        break
print('After batches, G count', current_frame.ascii.split('\n')[1].count('G'))
print('b count', current_frame.ascii.split('\n')[1].count('b'))
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
